*Submission 1 - Updated based on feedback*
Clean and organize the three data sets, Covar, Gene Expression, and Gene Names. The initial check will be to look and see if data is complete. All columns and row names will be logical, with the correct type assigned to each variable. The variables will be factored where necessary. Gene Expression was transposed and the probeID, or x, was renamed to be gene from Gene Names data. 

```{r}
#library(tidyverse)

#Set seed for Jitter function 
set.seed(100)

#Upload all raw data and store them as "Raw" variables
covar_raw <- read.csv("GSE85307_covar-1.csv")
geneExpress_raw <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneExpression.csv")
geneName_raw <- read.csv("GSE85307_geneNames.csv")

#View summary to see completeness of data, commented out for readability
#summary(covar_raw)
#summary(geneExpress_raw)
#summary(geneName_raw)
#No incomplete (NA) cases found

#Assign to a new variable to leave raw data untouched
covar <- covar_raw[complete.cases(covar_raw),]
geneExpress <- geneExpress_raw[complete.cases(geneExpress_raw),]
geneName <- geneName_raw[complete.cases(geneName_raw),]

#Clean Covar data
#Found .* in online resource, indexing each value to make sure 
##it only contains the numeric, text, or date value. 
###Factoring variables where necessary based on type. 
#head(covar)
covar$preg_preeclampsia <- factor(sub(".*: ","", covar$preg_preeclampsia), 
                                  levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia"))
covar$batch_Microarray  <- sub(".*: ", "", covar$batch_Microarray)
covar$batch_Microarray <- as.Date(as.character(covar$batch_Microarray), 
                                  format = "%m/%d/%Y")

for (row in 1:nrow(covar)) {
  for(col in 3:10){
    if(col == 4 | col == 7){ }
    else {covar[row,col]<- as.numeric(sub(".*: ","", covar[row,col]))}
  }
}
covar$mat_asthma <- factor(covar$mat_asthma, levels = c(0, 1), 
                           labels = c("Healthy", "Asthmatic"))


#Compare to Raw to confirm values were accurately translated, 
##commented out for readability
#head(covar)

#Rename columns to be more identifiable 
names(covar)[names(covar) == "mat_age_yrs"]  <- "age"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "preg_preeclampsia"]<- "Preeclampsia_status"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "delivery_gestAge_wks"]<- "delivery_wk"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "sampleCollection_gestAge_wks"] <- "collection_wk"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "batch_Microarray"] <- "collection_date"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "mat_BMI"]  <- "BMI"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "mat_vitD"] <- "vitD"
names(covar)[names(covar) == "mat_asthma"] <- "asthma_status"

#Prep for continuous to categorical data
covar$BMI_status <- ifelse(covar$BMI < 18.5, "Underweight",
                    ifelse(covar$BMI < 25, "Normal", ifelse(covar$BMI < 30, "Overweight", "Obese")))
covar$BMI_status <- factor(covar$BMI_status, 
                           levels = c("Underweight", "Normal", "Overweight", "Obese"))


#Check the result, commented out for readability
#head(covar)    

#Clean GeneExpressions:
#Rename X in geneExpression to the correct gene name from geneName, 
##rename col to gene
for (row_x in 1:nrow(geneExpress)) {
  for (row_gene in 1:nrow(geneName))
  if ( geneExpress[row_x, 1] ==geneName[row_gene,1]){
    geneExpress[row_x,1] <- geneName[row_gene, 2]
  }
}
names(geneExpress)[1] <- "gene"

#Confirm the gene name was translated correctly, commented out for readability
#head(geneExpress)

#Transpose geneExpress so each genes is a column
tp_geneExpress <- as.data.frame(t(geneExpress[, -1])) 

#Rename col names to the first row and remove the firstrow
names(tp_geneExpress) <- geneExpress$gene
tp_geneExpress$geoID <- rownames(tp_geneExpress)
rownames(tp_geneExpress) <- NULL

#Debugged this using AI since errors were occurring
covar[c(3, 5, 6, 8, 9)] <- lapply(covar[c(3, 5, 6, 8, 9)], as.numeric)  
tp_geneExpress <- tp_geneExpress[, c(ncol(tp_geneExpress), 
                                     1:(ncol(tp_geneExpress) - 1))]

#Check for correct transpose, commented out for readability
#head(tp_geneExpress)

#View summary to see completeness of all transformed data, 
##commented out for readability
#summary(covar)
#summary(tp_geneExpress)

merged_data <- merge(covar, tp_geneExpress, by ="geoID")
```

## Submission 1 Plots

```{r}
#Preparation for plots

#Define a theme
myTheme <- theme(
  # Remove grid lines and panel border
  panel.border     = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  # Axis text and lines
  axis.title       = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold", size = 14),
  axis.text        = element_text(color = "black", size = 12),
  axis.line        = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 1),
  # Backgrounds
  plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white"),
  panel.background = element_blank(),
  # Title and legend
  plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
  legend.position  = "bottom",
  legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
  legend.text      = element_text(size = 12),
  legend.key       = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "white"),
  # Geometry color
  geom = element_geom(color="black", fill="darkgrey")
)
```


Histogram of Gene Expression:

Histogram of TRIB1 Gene Expression

```{r}
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x=TRIB1))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = (mean(merged_data$TRIB1)+.03),color="black", 
             linewidth = 1, linetype="dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = (mean(merged_data$TRIB1)+0.03),y = Inf, 
           label = paste("Mean:",round(mean(merged_data$TRIB1), 1)),
           color = "black", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1,fontface = "bold") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = (median(merged_data$TRIB1)+.03),color="blue", 
             linewidth = 1, linetype="dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = (median(merged_data$TRIB1)+0.02),y = 19, 
           label = paste("Median:",round(median(merged_data$TRIB1), 1)),
           color = "blue", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1,fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = bquote(bold("Distribution of") ~ bolditalic("TRIB1") ~ bold("Expression")),
  x = bquote(bolditalic("TRIB1") ~ bold("Expression")), 
  y = "Number of Samples")+
  myTheme
```

Boxplot of Gene Expression Separated by Both Categorical Variables:

*Submission 2- Updated based on feedback*
Make a function to create hist, scatter, and boxplot by looping through 3 genes

```{r, fig.width = 9}

my_plotting_function <- function(data, list_of_genes, 
                    cont_var, cat_var, cat_cont_var )
  for(gene in list_of_genes){
    gene_mean   <- mean(as.numeric(paste(data[[gene]])))
    gene_median <- median(as.numeric(paste(data[[gene]])))
    
    #Histogram
    print(ggplot(data, aes(x=data[[gene]]))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05)+
  geom_vline(xintercept = (gene_mean+.03),color="black", 
             linewidth = 1, linetype="dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = gene_mean+0.03, y = Inf, 
           label = paste("Mean:",round(gene_mean, 1)),
           color = "black", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = (gene_median+.03),color="blue", 
             linewidth = 1, linetype="dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = (gene_median+0.03),y = Inf, 
           label = paste("Median:",round(gene_median, 1)),
           color = "blue", hjust = -0.1, 
           vjust = 3,fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = bquote(bold("Distribution of")~bolditalic(.(gene))~bold("Expression")),
       x = bquote(bolditalic(.(gene))~ bold("Expression")), 
       y = "Number of Samples")+
  myTheme)
    
    #Scatterplot
    print(ggplot(data, aes(x = data[[cont_var]], 
                           y = data[[gene]])) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm",formula = y~x, se = FALSE, 
              color = "black", 
              linewidth = 1.2) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, 
           label = paste("r =", 
                         round(cor(data[[cont_var]],
                                   data[[gene]]), 2)),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, fontface = "bold", color = "black")+
  labs(title = bquote(bolditalic(.(gene))~
                        bold("Expression vs. Maternal")~
                        bold(.(gsub("_", " ", cont_var)))), 
       x = paste0("Maternal ", gsub("_", " ", cont_var)), 
       y= bquote(bolditalic(.(gene))~
                   bold("Expression")))+
  myTheme)
    
    #Boxplot
   print(ggplot(data, aes(x = data[[cat_cont_var]] , 
                          y = data[[gene]], 
                        fill = data[[cat_var]]))+
  geom_boxplot( width = 0.7) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(
    jitter.width = 0.15,                     
    dodge.width = 0.8), 
             alpha = 0.5, size = 1.5, color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("white", "lightblue")) +
  labs(title = bquote(bolditalic(.(gene))~
                        bold("Expression by Maternal")~
                        bold(.(gsub("_status", "", cat_cont_var)))~ 
                        bold("and")~ bold(.(gsub("_s", " S", cat_var) ))),
       x = paste0("Maternal ",gsub("_s", " S", cat_cont_var)),
       y = bquote(bolditalic(.(gene))~ bold("Expression")), 
       fill = bquote(bold("Maternal") ~ bold(.(gsub("_s", " S", cat_var))))) +
  myTheme)
  }

my_plotting_function(merged_data, c("TRIB1", "SPAG9", "LGR4"), "BMI", "Preeclampsia_status", "BMI_status") 
```

Heatmap of Ten Gene Expressions by BMI and Preeclampsia Status
```{r}
#Pheatmap  (install.packages("pheatmap"))
#library(pheatmap)

ten_genes <- c("TRIB1", "LGR4", "SPAG9", "NFE2L1", 
               "KIF25-AS1", "SGK1", "MST1R", "BARD1", 
               "LRP10", "KRI1")

#reorganize the data to make it acceptable for a heatmap 
#make blank matrix of ten genes as rows and the geoID from merged data
genes_heatmap <- matrix (NA, nrow= length(ten_genes), ncol=nrow(merged_data))
rownames(genes_heatmap) <- ten_genes
colnames(genes_heatmap)<- merged_data$geoID

#fill each val from merged data in for each gene 
for (i in 1:length(ten_genes)){
  genes_heatmap[i,]<- merged_data[[ten_genes[i]]]
}

#tracking bars for the covars, make df of geoid, preeclampsia status, and bmi status
covars<- merged_data[, c("Preeclampsia_status", "BMI_status")]
rownames(covars) <- merged_data$geoID

#colors for tracking bars
covar_colors<- list(
  Preeclampsia_status = setNames(c("lightgrey", "darkgrey"), 
                levels(covars$Preeclampsia_status)),
  BMI_status = setNames(c("darkred", "orange", 
                          "darkgreen", "darkblue"),
                        levels(covars$BMI_status)))

#Generate heatmap, AI assistance used to fix the shaping, colors, 
##and scale of the heatmap to be visible
pheatmap(t(genes_heatmap),
         scale="column",
         clustering_distance_cols = 'euclidean',
         clustering_distance_rows = 'correlation',
         annotation_row =covars   ,
         annotation_colors = covar_colors,
         #scaling and shaping
         show_rownames  = FALSE,
         cellwidth      = 20,
         angle_col      = 45,
         treeheight_row = 40,
         treeheight_col = 40,
         fontsize_col   = 12,
         #no border
         border_color   = NA,
         #title
         main = "Expression of 10 Genes")
```
Additional Plot: Alluvial Plot of TRIB1 and BMI Status
```{r alluvial, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7}
#additional plot (install.packages("ggalluvial"))
#library(ggalluvial)
##Rgallery and AI Assistance used for understanding the inputs of this type of plot
#factor the TRIB1 level for visualization by above and below the median
merged_data$TRIB1_level <- factor(ifelse(merged_data$TRIB1
                                   >=median(merged_data$TRIB1),
  "High TRIB1", "Low TRIB1"),
                      levels = c("High TRIB1", "Low TRIB1"))

#create dateframe for this plot, make a table of counts 
##for expression in each BMI Category
alluvial_df <- as.data.frame(table(BMI_status = merged_data$BMI_status, 
                                   TRIB1_level = merged_data$TRIB1_level))

ggplot(alluvial_df, aes(axis1 = BMI_status, axis2 = TRIB1_level, y = Freq)) +
  #TRIB1 level on the right (1/4 the x axis), color by status
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = TRIB1_level), width = 1/4) +
  #BMI status on the left (1/4 the x axis)
  geom_stratum(width = 1/4, fill = "lightgrey", color = "black") +
  #apply the two strum
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Maternal BMI status", "TRIB1 level"), 
                   expand = c(0.15, 0.05)) +
  #create titles on each stratum
   geom_text(stat = "stratum",
             aes(label = ifelse(after_stat(count) > 10, 
                                (paste0(after_stat(stratum), 
                                        "\n(n = ", after_stat(count), ")")),
                                (paste0(after_stat(stratum), 
                                        " (n = ", after_stat(count), ")")))),
                 size = 3) +
  #scale colors
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("High TRIB1" = "darkred", 
                               "Low TRIB1" = "lightblue")) +
  #x and y labels
  labs(title = bquote(bold("Maternal BMI Status and")
                      ~ bolditalic("TRIB1")~bold("Level")),
       y = "Number of Samples", fill =
         bquote(bolditalic("TRIB1")~bold("Level"))) +
  myTheme
```
